spec.title: Shared origin
spec.text: When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

tokens.text: for every card that shares it

choices.question: How many is 'several' cards?

options.label: 3 or more cards, the alert's card included
2 or more
4 or more

choices.reason: 'Several' means more than two. The bank's own ring note (CC-2649: 'Two other cardholders reported the same device profile this month') treats three cards as a ring, and the agent's ring detectors use the same minimum (kavach.detectors.network.RING_MIN_CARDS = 3).

choices.question: When does a card 'show fraud' from the element?

options.label: precedent or atypical: a confirmed-fraud case opened before the decision holds one of its element transactions, or an element transaction is atypical for the card
atypical only
precedent only
atypical, a device marked New also counting

choices.reason: Fraud is only confirmed in the closed cases, so a confirmed case opened before the decision (not the alert's own) is the strongest reading; but a ring's newest victims have no case yet, so an element transaction that is atypical for the card's own history also counts (first use of the product, amount above every earlier one overall or for that product, first proxied connection: kavach.duckq_ext.card_atypical_window, the flags the typology detectors use). A device marked New is left out by default: it is common in normal traffic (onecard.py notes it does not separate fraud for most products).

choices.question: What is 'the same device profile'?

options.label: identical device_key, excluding placeholder and family-level profiles

choices.reason: device_key joins DeviceInfo, OS, browser and screen. A placeholder ('|||') or a family name such as 'Windows' or 'iOS Device' is shared by thousands of phones and is not one device: those are excluded with the agent's own test (kavach.detectors.network.generic_device: empty, on more than 100 cards, or a family name).

choices.question: Which rows carry 'the same billing region'?

options.label: addr1 on every row, any channel
addr1 on card-present rows only

choices.reason: addr1 is the billing region of the cardholder on every row; the rule says billing region, not place of purchase, so the literal reading keeps online rows (a regional breach shows up there). The typology detectors' card-present reading is measured as the alternative.

choices.question: What is 'the same recipient email'?

options.label: the same R_emaildomain (the data holds the domain only)

choices.reason: The index stores email domains, not addresses, so 'the same email' can only be the same domain; for free-mail domains this is weak, which the baseline condition below handles.

choices.question: How long is 'in one window'?

options.label: 14 days either side of the alert
7 days either side
3 days either side
30 days either side

choices.reason: The text gives no length. The bank's own confirmed ring ran 17.5 days from its first to its last confirmed card (the SM-G935F ring, CC-2649 to CC-3035), and an alert can come late in a ring, so the window must hold about two weeks of the ring's history before the alert; with the cutoff at the decision time, 14 days either side is in practice the 14 days before the alert. The agent's 7-day network window and 3 and 30 days are measured as alternatives.

measured.what: longest span, in days, between the first confirmed-fraud transactions of the cards of one bank ring (closed cases listing connected cards)

how.sql: with ring as (select c.case_id, unnest(string_split(c.card_id || '|' || c.connected_card_ids, '|')) card from closed c where c.connected_card_ids is not null and c.connected_card_ids <> ''), m as (select r.case_id, r.card, min(t.ts) first_ts from ring r join closed_txn ct on ct.card_id = r.card and ct.outcome = 'confirmed_fraud' join closed cc on cc.case_id = ct.case_id and cc.pattern = 'undocumented' join txn t on t.TransactionID = ct.TransactionID group by 1, 2) select max(span) from (select case_id, date_diff('hour', min(first_ts), max(first_ts)) / 24.0 span from m group by 1)

choices.question: Does sharing a common element (gmail.com, a big region) count?

options.label: only when the fraud-showing cards are at least 3 times the element's own baseline
no baseline condition
at least 5 times the baseline

choices.reason: The rule is silent, but 'the same billing region' or 'the same recipient email' identifies a shared origin only when more cards show fraud from it than usually do: gmail.com and the largest regions carry dozens of atypical purchases every week. The baseline is the mean number of cards showing fraud from that value per window over the 90 days before the window (complete windows inside the data only), scaled to the part of the window the cutoff leaves; with no baseline the value must be rare (100 cards or fewer in the window).

choices.question: Is the alert's own card one of the 'several'?

options.label: yes, when its flagged transaction carries the element

choices.reason: The alert is the reason to look; its card carries the element through the flagged transaction, and R6 is applied to that card's case. The other cards must show fraud on their own evidence.

choices.question: Which of the alert's elements are checked?

options.label: the values on the flagged transaction

choices.reason: R6 names the shared element of the alert; the flagged transaction's device profile, billing region and recipient domain are the candidates (earlier rows of the card would add values the alert is not about).

choices.phrase: for every card that shares it
choices.question: Which cards are 'every card that shares it'?

options.label: every card with the element in the window when the element is rare (100 cards or fewer); for a common element only the cards that show fraud from it

choices.chosen: all sharing cards for a rare element, else the fraud-showing ones
choices.reason: Taken literally for gmail.com the rule would put thousands of customers under monitoring; monitoring costs the customer nothing, but an analyst cannot act on thousands of names. Both counts are reported per hit.

choices.question: Which evidence may the rule see?

options.label: transactions and closed cases dated up to opened_at (reference anchors: anchor + the median delay)

choices.reason: Same cut as R5; the alert's own closed case never counts as precedent for itself.
